last_attempts_log.asr_text: I am for a rule at my daughter's high school. I would keep phones off during breaks and lunch too. Only banning them in class is not enough. I get home late from the job site. Fighting about phones every night makes me tired. If I can say, it's the school rule too, I won't be the only bad guy. My daughter did not keep our agreement. She was supposed to put her phone in the charging basket in the living room. I took her phone away. The next morning, it was hard to talk to her at breakfast. She also said, if I am the only one who replies late, I will be left out. I had no answer. I want her to keep our promise. I don't want to shout like my father either. But if she can't use her phone at school, nothing changes at home at night. Maybe I just want the school to help so my life is easier. I am a site supervisor who can't even manage things at home.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: First thing every morning, I see the kids who come to the nurse's office. I'm sleepy, they say. My head hurts, they say. The other day, a student was resting on the bed. Their phone screen glowed beside the pillow. When I hear they stayed up until morning, I don't know what to say. I also think about one student. After their phone was taken away at school, they stopped coming to see me. If they don't come, does that mean they are okay? A teacher asked me, if we ban phones, will fewer kids come to the nurse's office? I could not answer. If the school bans phones during breaks too, will it think the problem is solved? That scares me. I don't take phones away in the nurse's office. I wanna keep a place where kids can talk about what happened at night. After the phones are off limits, who will listen to that child?

last_attempts_log.asr_text: I'm against the rule that bans phones during breaks, too. I work at a warehouse during the day. At night, I go to evening high school. So I can't promise to stop all contact while I'm at school. Between classes, I get messages about my shifts. If I reply late, the work goes to someone else. Once, my workplace kept calling during class. I couldn't answer. Later, they told me it was a problem that they could not reach me. They almost cut my shifts, too. I want to graduate from this school. I also need money to give to my family. Now I can understand my classes. I don't want to choose between work and school. I promise to keep my phone at the bottom of my bag. I won't touch it during class. But before you decide, please hear how I work, too.
